sessions.title: Where Do You Live?
sessions.objective: Improve your ability to talk about where you live.
sessions.can_do: I can say where I live and describe my home area.
expressions: I live in a small apartment.
I've lived here for two years.
It takes ten minutes to walk to ___.
sessions.language_focus: Present simple; live in/near; for + time (introduced as a chunk)
sessions.pronunciation: Linking "live in"; stress on place words
sessions.task: Student and tutor interview each other about where they live, then summarize the partner's answers in three sentences. Student = new neighbor, Tutor = neighbor.
sessions.exit_task: Gives city, home type, and one neighborhood detail, and reports the partner's answer.
sessions.tutor_notes: Some learners are in temporary housing; accept "where I live now". Pay attention to "I am living" vs "I live".
challenge: Say where you live and how long.
Describe your street in three sentences.
Ask someone: "Where do you live?"
repair_phrases: Sorry, could you repeat that?
Could you speak a bit more slowly?
I didn't quite catch the last part.

sessions.unit_outcome: After this unit you can talk about where you live, why you are learning English, who you live with and what people look like.
sessions.title: Why Are You Learning English?
sessions.objective: Improve your ability to talk about learning English.
sessions.can_do: I can explain why I am learning English.
expressions: I've been studying for six months.
sessions.language_focus: because / to + verb of purpose; want/need/would like; present continuous for current study
sessions.pronunciation: Stress on the reason word; /tuː/ vs /tə/ in "to"
sessions.task: Student is interviewed by a program coordinator about their reasons and goals; then swaps. Student = applicant, Tutor = coordinator.
sessions.exit_task: Gives two reasons with because/to and one goal for next year.
sessions.tutor_notes: Reasons might be personal (asylum, work, family): welcome all. Use as a baseline to revisit in D051 and D106.
challenge: Say two reasons you are learning English.
Say what you want to do with English.
Ask someone why I learned a language.

sessions.objective: Improve your ability to talk about the people you live with.
sessions.can_do: I can talk about the people I live with.
expressions: There are five people in my family.
sessions.language_focus: live with; there are...; get along with; adverbs of frequency
sessions.pronunciation: /ð/ in "with the", "other"; sentence stress on the person word
sessions.task: Student introduces the people they live with using a "house members" card, and the tutor asks questions about each person. Student = speaker, Tutor = curious friend.
sessions.exit_task: Describes at least three household members with one fact each and answers follow-up questions.
sessions.tutor_notes: Family structures vary widely; avoid assumptions about parents/partners. Allow "I live alone".
challenge: Say who you live with.
Say one thing about each person.
Ask someone: "Who do you live with?"

sessions.objective: Improve your ability to describe people's appearance in detail.
sessions.can_do: I can describe people's appearance in detail.
expressions: He has a beard and a mustache.
sessions.language_focus: have/has + features; look like; adjective order (size + color); Does he have...?

sessions.exit_task: Describes a person using six features so the tutor picks the right photo from eight.
sessions.tutor_notes: Avoid body-shape judgments; use neutral physical description. "Look like" vs "look" (appearance vs similarity) is a common mix.
challenge: Describe a person in your family.
Describe your best friend's hair and face.
Ask someone: "Does he have a beard?"
